The version bump for v0.10.0, and its release notes.

- `launcher/package.json`, `launcher/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `launcher/Cargo.toml` (workspace version) and `launcher/Cargo.lock`: 0.9.0 → 0.10.0. The game's own version (`build_info::version()`, `port/cmake/BuildInfo.cmake`) is read from `tauri.conf.json`, so it follows. The SDK and the mods keep their versions.
- `launcher/release-notes/0.10.0.md`: everything since `launcher-v0.9.0`, the 99 commits of the old history (now in 6360471e) and #99–#114, for players and modders. merged.title: feat(launcher): mod updates at start, saved mod links, a mods mark on saves, and pad bindings
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
Four things players asked for: the launcher offers the mods' updates when it starts, Add a mod lists the links you already used, a save written with mods loaded is marked in the launcher and on the game's own memory card page, and the pad's sixteen buttons can be bound in the game's settings file.

merged.title: fix: Android full screen, lower input lag and rac1 visual fixes
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Android
- The game stays full screen and in landscape. This fixes the black bar above the picture at 16:9 on Vulkan, seen on the Retroid Pocket 6.
- The window and render threads get a performance hint session (ADPF), so the system sets clocks for the frame's work. `OPENRAC_ADPF_OFF` switches it off.
- The drawer has a new **Latency** card with Low-latency frames, Responsive camera and Responsive pad (`fresh_input`, which was in Sound and game before).

## Latency
- **Low-latency frames (Vulkan):** a frame between ticks sleeps before it starts, so it is queued just as the GPU becomes free. It no longer waits inside the frame for the frame before it. This also works with the render thread. The frame rate stays as it was, with lower input lag. The setting is on the game's Video page as well.

merged.title: fix(enhanced): Novalis water, probe profiles and bake inputs on the PAL disc
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Overview
The latest Enhanced graphics work (interior probe lighting, #119) was wired for NTSC-U only. PAL got the original water and baked with defaults. This brings PAL to the same state.

## Before
- Novalis enhanced water had hooks only in rac1-ntsc/host/water.c, and the frontend turned it on only for rac1-ntsc.
- bake_water.py read NTSC-U addresses only.
- Lighting and water profiles existed only for rac1-ntsc.
- Metropolis/Orxon static scenery, the Novalis pistons' travel and Gaspar's liquid bake input were limited to NTSC-U.

## After
PAL uses the same water and bake inputs as NTSC-U.

## How
- rac1-pal/host/water.c: the same hooks on PAL's functions, paired with NTSC-U's through games/rac1's function catalogue (same fingerprint, or same size and places). Data come from PAL's names.h (l01_packet_r, pool_tiles, scroll layers). Wrap rows added in libraries.tsv.
- The frontend gates accept any rac1-* disc.
- bake_water.py has an address table per disc. It picks the disc from the

merged.title: chore(import): sync rac1/ntsc to Lombyte f809a274
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Overview
Syncs games/rac1/ntsc to Lombyte f809a274 and adapts the port to the new layout.

- Import by a 3-way merge with rename detection (OpenRAC's tree at the recorded commit merged with Lombyte main). Hunks git could not place were carried by hand to the function with the same label; every patch line is present exactly once.
- OPENRAC_PATCHES.md: paths follow the new files. Rows Lombyte now covers itself are dropped (load_level_gameplay, random_float_between, random_angle_radians, sharkigator, 003054b0, bolt_thief/bomb, batalia_deserter, camera_object, FUN_L14_00307a80).
- port_symbols.txt: release_voice_slot, which new L04 class files call by plain name (the port was calling an empty stub).
- hostgen: skip list and drafts follow src/sdk/soft_float and src/sdk/libc; `__typeof__(NAME)` renamed with the va builtins (vfprintf.c was unreadable); the flickering-mesh override follows flickering_mesh_effect.c with VLAs as alloca.

## Testing
- hostgen: 0 unreadable units, 0 ho

merged.title: ci(launcher): skip the launcher build on pull requests
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
`launcher.yml` ran on `pull_request` for every target branch except `develop` (so in practice release PRs `develop` -> `master` and PRs into other branches), building the whole matrix (Windows, Linux x86_64/ARM64, Fedora, macOS, Android) on top of the build the push already does.

## After
Pull requests no longer trigger `launcher`. It still runs on pushes to `master`/`develop` (dev release), on `launcher-v*` tags (release drafts) and by hand (`workflow_dispatch`).

## How
- Dropped the `pull_request` trigger (and the now unused `&paths` anchor).
- Removed the dead `github.event_name != 'pull_request'` conditions in the version step and the `dev-release` job, and updated the comments that mentioned pull request builds.
- Nothing else depends on PR runs: `publish.yml` listens to `launcher` via `workflow_run`, but only acts on tag drafts, and `checks.yml` is untouched.

Note for maintainers: if branch protection on `master` lists any `launcher` matrix job as a required check, r

merged.title: fix(launcher): let a development build switch back to an older Stable release
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
Choosing Stable on a development build only took a release newer than the build, so with the latest release older than the installed X.Y.Z-dev.N the launcher said it was up to date and never went back. On the other channel than the one it was built for, the launcher is now offered that channel's build whatever its version (update::offered), shown as "Switch to Stable X.Y.Z". Its own channel still takes only newer builds.

Android installs no lower version code over a higher one, so there the switch to an older release sends the player to the release's APK, to install after uninstalling the launcher with its data kept.

merged.title: fix(hostgen): run moby updates again after the Lombyte sync
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
The NTSC decomp now writes the moby update loops' call (`if (update) update(moby);`) as a jalr in the MOBY_CALL_UPDATE macro (include/moby_update.h). Clang's JSON has no text for an asm statement spelled through a macro, so hostgen turned it into a bare barrier and reported nothing: update_visible_mobys, link_and_update_all_mobys and update_all_mobys_profiled stopped calling any moby's update. On Novalis the pond's moby never initialised its 21 tiles, so the still water was missing.

- rac1-ntsc hostgen.json: MOBY_CALL_UPDATE given as C, its header guard defined (as qzero's), so the loops call the update again.
- hostgen reads the text of asm statements spelled in a header or a macro, and reports one it still cannot read, so such a loss is no longer silent (report.json inline_assembly_skipped).
- hostgen translates a lone `sw %N,%M` to a memory output (func_0012C4C8, the MPEG frame size update).
- Override for draw_vendor_effects: the matching C hands d0 to the second euler_rotation_ba

merged.title: fix: Responsive controls camera at any frame rate, and low-latency frames at the display's rate
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before

- With Responsive camera on and one frame a tick (a frame cap of 60 on NTSC's 60 ticks), the camera stood still while the right stick was held, then sprang to where it should have been. The latch's fade expected the picture to keep turning at the rate the picture itself had turned; with every frame a new tick the carry held the picture still, that rate stayed zero, and the picture froze until the step grew past the cut threshold (0.6 rad) and jumped.
- Letting go of the stick, the latch switched off while the game's camera was still easing out its turn, so the picture turned back by the latch's lead (about 4°).
- Low-latency frames with VSync showed 60 fps on a 120 Hz display: on Android, Vulkan's two swapchain images made every frame wait a refresh for SurfaceFlinger to release one; on OpenGL, between() rejected every frame shown at or after the next tick, though the next tick's own frame comes a refresh later.
- Responsive camera was on by default; Responsive pad and Respo

merged.title: fix(port): mobys drawn in the 2D path no longer sample with its sampler
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody: The mobys the game renders into a target (the vendor's item and salesman screens, the menu pages' item previews) are drawn from inside the 2D path's draw list, while that path's sampler object was still bound to units 0 and 1. A bound sampler overrides a texture's own wrap and filter, so those mobys sampled with whatever the last 2D draw used, mostly clamped. The Pyrocitor's texture coordinates run from 1 to 2 (the GS repeats its texture), so on the vendor's screen it took its texture's edge texels all over and showed grey. The samplers are unbound before the mobys are drawn and bound again by the next 2D draw.

opened.untrustedBody: The mobys the game renders into a target (the vendor's item and salesman screens, the menu pages' item previews) are drawn from inside the 2D path's draw list, while that path's sampler object was still bound to units 0 and 1. A bound sampler overrides a texture's own wrap and filter, so those mobys sampled with whatever the last 2D draw used, mostly clamped. The Pyrocitor's texture coordinates run from 1 to 2 (the GS repeats its texture), so on the vendor's screen it took its texture's edge texels all over and showed grey. The samplers are unbound before the mobys are drawn and bound again by the next 2D draw.

opened.title: feat(src): classify func_002A1130 as handwritten
opened.author: cadelass
opened.untrustedBody:
The 584-byte body at 0x002A1130 uses instructions the compiler never emits: $at as a
working register (lhu $at, mtc1 $at, beqz $at, addi $at), and trapping add/addi
throughout where the compiler would emit addu/addiu. It also jumps into its own middle
and ends with a tail jump to func_002A1378 instead of returning. Mark it ASM_FUNC
under the second criterion of AGENTS.md "Handwritten assembly", which needs a
maintainer's agreement in review.

Checks: python3 tests/check_repository.py (repository checks passed);
python3 tools/progress.py --check (one original-assembly function awaits the
maintainer's report refresh); git diff --check passed. The unit tests give the same
15 environment errors with and without this change. ASM_FUNC and INCLUDE_ASM expand
to the same thing (include/include_asm.h), so the linked programs are unchanged; the
strict build was not run.

opened.title: docs(nonmatching): func_0034F048, the movie playback loop at 876/880 bytes
opened.author: cadelass
opened.untrustedBody:
Retains a near miss for `func_0034F048` (880 bytes, boot and all 27 levels): the movie playback loop that `func_0034EF58` calls after the movie is set up. It returns whether the player skipped the movie.

## What differs

Everything matches except the skip-button test. Retail loads `D_001A7478` once into `v1` and copies it to `a1` (`beq v1,s1` / `daddu a1,v1`), and sets `skip = 1` in the delay slots of a `beql pressed,zero` and a `bnez 0x800`, which then fall through to the 64-bit combo test. With this C, cc1 keeps the address of `D_001A7478` (it reloads the value for the `!= 0` test) and shares one `skip = 1` block. The result is one instruction shorter.

Variants tried (sizes from `tools/check.py`):
- a block-local `mode` copy: 868
- `mode` assigned in the condition: 868
- the three cases as one `||` expression: 876, but the saved registers shift
- the combo as a plain assignment: `sltiu` instead of retail's `movn`

`src/` keeps the `INCLUDE_ASM` marker; the draft is in `nonmatching/

Retains a near miss for `func_L01_003D8830` (672 bytes, level 01 only): it spawns `count` particles on a ring around an object, with its settings in `D_L01_002A4E78`.

## What differs

Two load orders still differ:
- at entry, retail loads `startColor` (`lw $fp`) before spilling `obj` (`sw $a0,0x40($sp)`); cc1 spills first
- after `func_00282CC0`, retail loads `pos[2]` before `cfg.height`; cc1 loads `height` first

opened.title: docs(nonmatching): func_002D6230, the text-list drawer at 1696/1700 bytes
opened.author: cadelass
opened.untrustedBody:
Retains a near miss for `func_002D6230` (1700 bytes, boot and all 27 levels). It draws the `ListMenu` that `func_002D5EC0` handles: each entry's label centred, a shadow pass offset by `D_001AA444`/`D_001AA448` and a colour pass. On the control-binding lists (`D_00259148`…`D_002592D8`) it prints the bound button with the label through `D_001ABAC8`. It returns 1 when the list switches to the small font to fit, else 2.

## What differs

The draft goes at the end of `src/game/002D5E98-list-g8.c`, with `width` at 0x20 and `height` at 0x24 added to `ListMenu`. `func_002D5EC0` stays 28/28 there. The frame, the colour choice and the binding lookup match. Only register allocation differs (MATCHING-BLOCKERS 1): retail keeps `menu` in s3 and `y` in fp and spills `i + 1` to `0x18($sp)`; cc1 puts `menu` in s2 and spills `y`.
